newsitem.title: USA: American Stores to buy back $550 mln of shrs.
newsitem.headline: American Stores to buy back $550 mln of shrs.

text.p: American Stores Co said Friday it agreed to repurchase from the family of L. S. Skaggs and certain family and charitable trusts 12.2 million of its common shares at $45 a share or about $550 million.

The company said it plans to finance the share repurchase, initially through bank lines of credit. Subject to market conditions, it said it expects to refinance the buyback in public stock or debt offerings or both over the next six to twelve months.

The company said it also agreed to file a registration statement with regulators to enable such shareholders to sell between 14.7 million and 16.4 million additional shares in a secondary offering as promptly as practicable.

American Stores, one of the nation's largest food and drug retailers, said the repurchase aims to further the best interest of the company, while permitting the orderly sale by the Skaggs family and trusts of their holding in the company's stock.
Victor L. Lund, chairman and chief executive officer of the company, said the repurchase will slightly add to American Stores' earnings per share, and will not affect its capital expenditure program.

A spokesman for the Skaggs family, the company's largest shareholder, said, "We are pleased that we have been able to reach an agreement with American Stores with respect to our holdings," addding the family's objective has always been to enhance long term shareholder value."
The closing of the share repurchase is expected to occur simultaneously with the closing of the secondary offering.

If the price to the public in the secondary offering would be less than $45 per share, the selling stockholders have the right to terminate the secondary offering and, if they also elect, the company repurchase.

It said either American Stores or the selling stockholders may terminate the transactions if they are not consummated within 60 days following the date the company files a registration statement for the secondary offering.
The selling stockholders have agreed to enter into a 10-year standstill agreement restricting purchases and sales of the company's shares, proxy fights and other actions.

If neither the share repurchase nor the secondary offering is consummated, the standstill period would be reduced to 30 months. The company has also granted the selling stockholders certain registration rights during the standstill period.

American Stores operates 1,695 stores in 26 states. Its principal retail operations include Acme Markets, Jewel Food Stores, Lucky Northern California Division, Lucky Southern California Division, Jewel Osco Southwest, and Osco and Sav-on drug stores.
